div.head: II Cn 68.2
div.ab: Eac on mænigre dæde, þonne man byð nydwyrhta, þonne byð se gebeorges þe bet wyrðe, þe he for neode dyde þæt þæt he dyde.
Eac on manigre dæde, þonne man byð nydwyrhta, þonne bið se gebeorges þe bet wyrðe, þe he for neode dyde þæt þæt he dyde.
Item in multis, quando aliquis coactus peccat, magis uenia dignus (ueniale) est, si necessitate fecit quod fecit.
Eac on gemeanre dæde ðonne man bið nydwyrhta, ðonne bið se man ðe bet wyrðe gebeorges, ðe he for neode dyde þæt þæt he dyde.
Eac on mænigre dæde, þonne man byð nydwyrhta, þonne byð se gebeorges þe bet wyrðe, þe he for neode dyde þæt þæt he dyde.
Likewise, in many cases of evil-doing, when a man is an involuntary agent, he is more entitled to clemency because he acted as he did from compulsion.
Moreover, in many cases, when the criminal has acted out of compulsion, then he is more deserving of leniency because he did what he did out of necessity.
Also in many a deed, when a man acts under compulsion, he is then the more entitled to protection in that he did what he did out of necessity.
Ferner bei mancher (gemeinsamer B) Missethat, wenn jemand Zwangsthäter [gewesen] ist, dann ist dieser (Mann B) Schutzes um so eher werth, je mehr er was er that, aus Zwang gethan hat.
Further, in many a (joint, B) misdeed, when someone [has been] a doer under compulsion, then this (man, B) is the more worthy of protection, the more he has done what he did out of compulsion.
div.note: Liebermann compares Canons of Edgar, Confessional 4.
mænigre: gemeanre B þonne byð . . . wyrðe: ðonne bið se man ðe bet wyrðe B
